# A stable Kramers HS identity whose continued determinant has the wrong trace

## 1. Precise statement and primary boundary

Consider a single site with two unconstrained boson modes a=(b,c). Let N=a^dagger a and S_j=a^dagger sigma_j a, j=x,y,z. At beta=1 choose

`H = S_x^2+S_y^2+S_z^2 - N^2/2`.

This is a stable Hamiltonian with a finite, unambiguous grand-canonical partition function. It admits an exact continuous Gaussian/compact-group HS identity, sector by sector, all of whose one-body histories have Kramers symmetry and a positive algebraic inverse determinant. Nevertheless integrating that continued determinant does NOT yield the physical partition function: the proposed result is less than 7/9, while the physical result is greater than one.

The controlling claim tested is the post-continuum finite-part recovery identity in Yu–Wei–Li **arXiv:2610.31541v1**, SM section IV, equations (S95)–(S103), especially (S101) and (S103). The stated input there is a stable many-body Hamiltonian with finite grand-canonical trace; the treatment expressly allows field histories with divergent bare traces. Its starting interaction class in SM (S1) is a sum of squares of Hermitian one-body operators, with either sign, and (S3)/(S4) give their real/imaginary Gaussian decouplings. No commutativity of different channels is assumed there. The present H has exactly four such channels, with coefficients +1,+1,+1,-1/2 and quadratic H0=0.

The configuration-level Kramers determinant sign statement, SM (S111)–(S113), remains true. The counter does not reject trace-convergent implementations, the valid U2=0 lattice models, canonical coefficient recurrences, or all positive representations of this Hamiltonian. This one-site physical model has an ordinary positive occupation representation.

**Limit boundary:** the exact continuous HS identity below is used directly. We do NOT claim that a particular finite Gaussian-slice determinant expectation converges to our answer. Its kernel is unbounded near a determinant zero, so weak convergence of the group products alone would not pay that extra limit or trace-norm convergence. The counter targets a general post-continuum finite-part completion, not the numerically reported finite-slice solver's unqualified limiting value.

# Root review of the stable continuous finite-part counter

Root whole-read a_independent/canonical_boson/STABLE_FINITE_PART_COUNTER.md,
regularization_counter.py and STABLE_COUNTER.json, and directly read the
governing primary SM sectionIV equationsS95--S103. ACCEPTED at the exact
continuous quadratic-history/post-continuum scope,29October2026.

The Schwinger calculation includes normal ordering: sum S_j^2=N(N+2), so the
actual Hamiltonian is N^2/2+2N, with vacuum energy zero, finite partition and
positive n=1 contribution. The three repulsive one-body Gaussian spin channels
generate SU2 Brownian motion with representation mean exp[-n(n+2)]I. The
independent attractive scalar channel contributes exp(n^2/2), giving exactly
exp(-H) on every finite-particle sector and a unique trace-class extension.
This is a valid sectorwise HS identity, not a trace-class Bochner integral.

Every one-body history e^s U has the stated Kramers symmetry. Its continued
inverse determinant is positive. Inside spectral radius one its averaged
character expansion is absolutely valid; outside it determinant reciprocity
gives r^-2 F(1/r). Gaussian half-line integration therefore yields the stated
J(n)+J(n+2) series. Monotonic J, J2<1/5 and the elementary exponential-series
bound prove Zdet<280/361<1<Zphysical. Numerical quadrature is not a premise.

Root independently recomputed the convergent series read-only at70 digits:
Zphysical=1.17171696326686319004334162559939783358 and
Zdet=0.70651251271087812194383106680949388281. Exact Fraction checks also
confirmed exp(3)>20 and39/361<1/9. The producer's finite Casimir controls and
these numerical series check implementation scope; the all-n proof is analytic.

The primary expressly begins the tested recovery claim with a stable H and
finite physical partition, allowing divergent individual bare field traces.
The counter isolates the missing interchange of field integration, occupation
sum and finite-part extraction. Configuration-level Kramers positivity itself
remains correct. Trace-convergent implementations and the separately constructed
balanced canonical class are not rejected. Historical priority is UNKNOWN.

Root raised and the producer preserved a decisive limit qualification: weak
convergence of finite Gaussian spin products does NOT alone give convergence
